assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration turned electron microscopy into a routine sub-angstrom, atom-by-atom probe of interfaces, defects and functional materials; this is a clear, original instrument invention with enormous lasting impact across physics, chemistry and materials science. From my own TEM and spectroscopy vantage I see its consequences in daily practice.
assessment.attribution: The decisive trio is well delineated: Rose's multipole corrector design, Haider and Urban's implementation and demonstration of working correctors in TEM and STEM. Other groups (e.g. Krivanek and collaborators in STEM) also contributed, but the supplied credit supports a coherent three-person configuration; allocation relative to the STEM branch is not fully resolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature: commercial aberration-corrected instruments have been widespread for over twenty years and independently confirmed by thousands of results. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the STEM-corrector pioneers outside the credited names deserve equal weight is uncertain.
Some may see it as an enabling tool rather than a discovery, though the prize criteria explicitly include inventions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, a large, fast-growing field with clear conceptual novelty and strong tunability.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic-angle flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive experiments. The theory-plus-experiment pairing is natural. Other contributors (e.g. the Cao/Fatemi/Jarillo-Herrero team members, other theory groups) complicate a strict three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: reproduced by many groups and extended to other moire systems since 2018, although the nature of the superconducting pairing remains debated.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and the full phase diagram are still not settled.
Credit among junior experimental authors and other early theorists is not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reached uncertainties near 1e-18 and enable relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental physics; a clear invention with transformative metrology impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice clock; Ye drove the record-precision implementations. Two laureates give a clean configuration, though Hall and Hansch were already honoured in 2005 for the frequency comb underpinning this work.
assessment.maturity: Mature in performance and independently reproduced by many national laboratories; the redefinition of the second is still pending, which is not a barrier to recognition.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier frequency-metrology recognition may reduce novelty in the committee's eyes.
Ye's role is also credited elsewhere on the longlist (thorium clock), which does not affect this entry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and giant MgO-based junctions underpin hard-disk read heads and magnetic memory; discovery and subsequent materials engineering were both important, with a direct materials and interface-quality dimension I know well.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported large room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin's group and others (notably Yuasa and collaborators, not on the credited list) established coherent tunnelling through crystalline MgO. A fair configuration among the credited names is plausible but some key contributors are absent.
assessment.maturity: Very mature; technology has been in use for more than fifteen years and the physics is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Missing credit for the MgO coherent-tunnelling contributors is a real gap.
Spintronics was recognised in 2007 (GMR), which may be seen as partial overlap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a major paradigm: topological classification of band structures with experimental realisations. Broad and lasting influence on condensed matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theoretical proposal; Molenkamp's group demonstrated the effect in HgTe quantum wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, which is not credited here, and others (e.g. Zhang, Hasan) have strong claims. The allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent confirmations in 2D and 3D materials, though practical applications remain limited.
uncertainties: Credit is contested among several theorists and experimentalists outside the supplied names.
Topological phases already recognised in 2016 may raise the bar for novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised Hubbard models in a controllable way and observed the superfluid-Mott transition, a conceptually clear and widely adopted approach to many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and collaborators proposed the Hubbard-model realisation; Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott transition experiment, and Esslinger's fermionic work is also essential. Limiting to three laureates forces a hard choice that remains unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a method, though the long-term scientific payoff for solving open problems such as high-Tc is still developing. BEC prize of 2001 and later tools reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Choice among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger and Zoller is difficult.
Whether quantum simulation has yet delivered a decisive discovery is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provides the architecture for superconducting quantum processors and strong light-matter coupling on chip, an invention with large influence across quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf and collaborators proposed and implemented the architecture; Wallraff's 2004 experiment demonstrated strong coupling. The credited list has four names, so a three-person selection requires omitting someone.
assessment.maturity: Maturing quickly through widespread reproduction; the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits makes timing sensitive.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recently recognised superconducting-circuit work.
Which of Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and Wallraff to omit is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recollision (three-step) model and quantum theory of high-harmonic generation underlie attosecond science and are a clear, important conceptual advance.
assessment.attribution: Corkum's semiclassical model and Lewenstein's quantum theory are decisive; Schafer's contemporaneous work on above-threshold ionisation is also relevant. Attribution is reasonable but partly adjacent to the 2023 prize.
assessment.maturity: Mature and heavily confirmed through attosecond experiments; however, the 2023 prize already honoured the experimental side, so recognition of the theory could look duplicative.
uncertainties: Relative credit between Corkum, Schafer and Lewenstein for the model is not fully settled.
